newsitem.title: USA: News Corp. investment in EchoStar delayed.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. investment in EchoStar delayed.

text.p: Australian conglomerate News Corp. Ltd's application for regulatory approval of its planned $1 billion investment in satellite company EchoStar Communications Corp. has been delayed, Echostar said on Monday.
News Corp. told EchoStar on Friday that it was setting new conditions for its agreement to make the investment, Echostar said in a news release.

News Corp. has asked EchoStar to abandon its existing system of consumer access to satellite-delivered television programs and replace it with a system provided by News Corp. EchoStar said it has requested additional information from News Corp. to further consider whether the News Corp. system can meet criteria spelled out in their binding agreement.
News Corp. also told EchoStar it believes other matters must be resolved as well, but Echostar didn't say what those items were.

EchoStar had said Friday that it expected the $1 billion venture to proceed in accordance with the binding agreement. EchoStar was responding to an article casting doubts about the deal and alleging that News Corp. may be looking at other possible partners.

However, EchoStar said Monday that while it hopes News Corp. will honor its obligations under the agreement, a new timetable for regulatory filings has not been set and there can be no assurance that News Corp. will proceed with the planned investment. The companies had planned to submit U.S. regulatory filings by the end of April.
